thread.title: Fitbit: Amid Long-Term Questions, a New Smartwatch

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Fitbit: Amid Long-Term Questions, a New Smartwatch
text:
Photo: Fitbit The shift from fitness trackers to smartwatches has been tough to ignore—and it’s been particularly tough on companies such as Fitbit , which saw its market share in wearables tumble last year . 
On Tuesday, the Barron’s Next 50 stock announced new products it hopes will help revitalize its position . They included the new $200 Versa, a device that advertises health monitoring—and, notably, female-focused functions including menstrual tracking—music and other apps. (They also included a new $99 fitness tracker for kids.)
But there hasn’t been a lot of investor optimism around Fitbit (FIT) lately, with hard-charging competition in the wearables space, particularly from tech behemoth Apple (AAPL). “We don’t yet see a path to profitability and are challenged to make a compelling upside case for Fitbit shares,” Stifel analysts wrote last month. 
• Fitbit shipped the most wearables, and had the largest market share in the category, as recently as 2016. That hasn’t held. Expense management—and, perhaps, acquisitions that bolster Fitbit’s ability to cast itself as an innovator that makes devices appealing, and useful, enough to be essential alternatives to the Apple Watch, among others—could revive the bull case. 
• Healthcare is seen as one way it could do that—eventually. “The company has an excellent opportunity ahead with medical applications,” Wedbush wrote last month, “but it is unlikely that subscription revenue will contribute meaningfully before 2019.”
Of course, product launches that keep it relevant in a growing category could help too. Fitbit shares were up some 2% early Tuesday afternoon; investors appear intrigued by today’s announcements, at the very least. 
• Meanwhile, the outlook for fitness trackers cooled further Tuesday as Dick’s Sporting Goods CEO Edward Stack, speaking on a conference call — a transcript of which was made available by FactSet — said his company would be “significantly reducing” its commitment to that business. 
“The sales are continuing to go down,” Stack said. “We can find a better use for that square footage in our store, so we’re significantly reducing our investment there.”
